works.abstract: Marine plastics have become one of the most pervasive and complex environmental challenges of our time, impacting ecosystems, wildlife, and human communities across the globe and representing a critical topic for marine science education. This paper describes a place-based professional development workshop for high school teachers held at the Wrigley Marine Science Center on Catalina Island centered on microplastics and marine debris. Teachers engaged in a sequence of hands-on learning stations supported by instructional handouts and accessible materials including: (1) examination of plankton and plastic samples collected from the North Pacific Gyre, (2) sink-and-float experiments investigating plastic density and material properties, (3) geospatial tracking of marine debris using mapping by coordinates, (4) sorting of sand into natural versus synthetic components, (5) microfiber detection using phone adapter microscopes, and (6) a nylon polymer chemistry demonstration. Written participant reflections were analyzed using qualitative thematic coding. Emergent themes included increased content understanding of polymer science and microplastic pathways, strengthened confidence in teaching complex and emerging environmental issues, appreciation for the nylon chemistry demonstration as an anchoring phenomenon, and intentions to implement or adapt multiple investigations in high school science courses. Findings suggest that immersive, phenomena-based professional development that integrates polymer chemistry, real-world marine samples, and quantifiable investigation stations can strengthen secondary teachers’ ability to connect abstract chemical and environmental principles to large-scale ocean systems. The results further indicate that station-based design, use of authentic field-collected materials, and cross-institutional partnerships create a replicable model for marine education programs seeking to integrate chemistry, environmental science, and student action projects within NGSS-aligned secondary curricula.

works.title: Teaching Marine Debris: A Professional Development Model for Integrating Microplastics Science into Secondary Education
